principle: Size and risk are SEPARATE axes. Risk is the DOMINANT axis: a 3-line change can be CRITICAL. Risk classification reuses the existing canonical enum from src/risk-normalization.mjs (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL) — admission's risk axis is the SAME single authority, never a second enum. Unknown or unverifiable signals escalate (fail-closed); insufficient evidence never default-allows.

tiers.label: low
tiers.meaning: No signal in any risk class; read-only or reversible local effect; no secrets, no production/runtime effect, no persistence, no external system
tiers.lifecycleEffect: fast path eligible (only with size XS/S); direct execution; evidence lightweight

tiers.label: medium
tiers.meaning: ≥1 MEDIUM-class signal OR any signal present but not clearly classified; local mutation of non-governed code; standard isolation + review strength
tiers.lifecycleEffect: writer needs worktree isolation; review = deterministic verify or independent review at discretion; no external review by default

tiers.label: high
tiers.meaning: ≥2 MEDIUM signals OR ≥1 HIGH-class signal (see signals); strict-reviewer routing (isStrictReviewRisk); governed/lifecycle code, persistence, database mutation, security-boundary-adjacent, concurrency
tiers.lifecycleEffect: strict independent review REQUIRED; durable execution recommended; no fast path; controller gate for external effects; repair budget bounded; evidence persistent

tiers.label: critical
tiers.meaning: ≥1 CRITICAL-class signal OR ≥2 HIGH signals OR any unverifiable signal with destructive potential; secrets/credentials, destructive writes, irreversible actions, production/runtime effects, external publishing, commit/push/merge/release, self-modification, memory write-back, remote/network write
tiers.lifecycleEffect: human/controller gate REQUIRED before execution; independent review REQUIRED; external review REQUIRED; durable execution + checkpoint REQUIRED; memory write-back DENIED unless explicitly admitted; no direct execution; decomposition REQUIRED

examples: rm -rf, destructive migration, truncate, overwrite of production artifact

riskSignals.evidenceRequired: no secret may ever enter evidence/telemetry/memory

riskSignals.note: same class as RS.SECRETS; kept separate for inventory precision

examples: fetch/push/pull to remote, external API calls
touches production scheduler, runtime adapters, live services
schema change, migration, durable store layout, checkpoint format
any write/delete/update to a database (incl. memory sqlite store)
authn/authz, sandbox, secret scan, permission model, pi adapter tool policy
leases, locks, parallel workers, race-prone state, writer serialization
lifecycle-authorization, review-unit gate, closeout, delivery, review-bundle inventory
task modifies its own admission, scheduler, authority, or governance code
any write to Codebase Memory (trust ladder, records)
no rollback path, one-way migrations, external irreversible publish
release, publish package, push branch/PR, deploy to any remote

escalationRules: any CRITICAL signal -> CRITICAL (regardless of count, size, or intent)
any signal with UNVERIFIABLE classification and destructive potential -> escalate one tier above the best guess (fail-closed), minimum HIGH
insufficient evidence overall -> minimum MEDIUM, never LOW (default-deny)
signal inventory is part of the admission record (reasons) so the tier is explainable and auditable
escalation is MONOTONIC: no later refinement may lower a tier below the original unless new verifiable evidence contradicts a specific signal (documented, controller-approved for CRITICAL)
risk tier is FROZEN once execution begins; drift -> HOLD (admission drift guard)

separationContract.sizeNeverLowersRisk: size classification can only raise lifecycle weight, never lower risk tier
separationContract.riskDominatesWeight: lifecycle profile is chosen as risk tier first, then size refines weight WITHIN the tier
separationContract.fastPathGuard: fast path requires risk LOW AND size XS/S; a HIGH-risk XS task uses the HIGH profile, not the fast path

examples.lifecycle: HIGH profile (strict review, durable, no fast path)
